# Tech Team Draft (weekly recap)

First-run setup is the tech-team-draft-getting-started skill. This skill is the weekly run.

## Rules
- Read-only. Use only Grok Bot's built-in read-only `x` tools: get_users_by_usernames, get_users_posts, search_posts_all. No other X tool, no user-connected X account.
- Never post, reply, like, repost, follow, bookmark or DM. The recap goes only back to the user in chat.
- Never invent handles, bios, posts, links or numbers. Every name, quote, like count and post count comes from this run's X responses. Zero posts: `quiet week`. Handle not found: `no data`.
- Quotes are verbatim, 20 words or fewer, each linked to https://x.com/<handle>/status/<id>.
- Roster: exactly 5 starters, bench 0 to 6, 11 max, no duplicates, every handle from the working pool (seed table below plus refresh adds).
- This skill is self-contained: everything it needs is in this file. It needs no other files. State lives only in your memory or the one state file you create (see Lineup state).

## Player pool seed (29 handles, order = tile numbers 1 to 29)
Public X accounts only. Flags: `initials` = show initials, not the avatar (official/logo accounts). `former` = bio says previously at xAI. `no-bio-affil` = bio does not state the affiliation. FOUNDER = the public X bio says founder/co-founder/founding team (quoted); no other player gets the tag.

## Weekly pool refresh (each Sunday, before picking starters)
The pool table above is the seed. The working pool lives in your own memory or in a file you create (the `pool` field of the lineup state); on first run, copy the seed. Refresh it every Sunday before picking starters:
1. Find up to 3 new candidates with one read-only search_posts_all for the last 7 days, query exactly `<GOAL_OR> (SpaceX OR xAI OR SpaceXAI OR SpaceXSI) -is:retweet -is:reply -is:quote -has:cashtags`, max_results 25 (the most one call returns), expansions author_id, user.fields description,username,name,protected,most_recent_tweet_id,profile_image_url. Add an author only if all hold: public (not protected), not already in the pool, their bio shows a SpaceX or xAI affiliation, and they posted on the goal this week (an on-topic post per the picking rules; "bot" alone does not count). No affiliation evidence in the bio means no add, however popular the post.
   - Affiliation counts only as an @mention (`@SpaceX`, `@SpaceXAI`, `@SpaceXSI`, `@xAI`, any case) or a work phrase naming one of them (`at @SpaceXAI`, `building @…`, `engineer at …`, `engineering at …`, `working at …`, `designing …`, `researcher at …`). A bare word ("SpaceX fan", "I love xAI") is not affiliation.
   - Never add a ticker, maxi or investor bio, even with a mention: reject any bio with a cashtag (`$SPCX`, `$TSLA`, ...), `maxi`, `investor` or `shareholder`. Example: a bio "SpaceX, Tesla maxi ... $SPCX alpha" (like @spcxGOD) is rejected. Rank by on-topic post count, then likes; take at most 3.
2. Drop players with no post in the last 30 days, judged from `most_recent_tweet_id` in this week's get_users_by_usernames call (post time = (id >> 22) + 1288834974657 ms). Never drop one of last week's starters or bench players. On the first run (no week entry yet) skip drops entirely, and also while the state has only a setup entry (no `weekly` entry yet): drops start with the second weekly-or-later run, after the first `weekly` entry exists. Missing activity data is never a drop.
3. Never over 35: adds stop when the pool reaches 35. Refill: while the pool is under 29, re-add retired seed players (seed order) whose `most_recent_tweet_id` in this week's lookup is within 30 days; they get their old tile numbers back and show as `+@handle` on the Pool line. Call 1 therefore looks up the working pool plus any retired seed players (one batch).
4. Empty or failed search: the pool stays exactly as it was this week (no adds, no drops). Empty goal: skip the search (no adds); drops and refill still apply.
5. Budget: the refresh uses at most 2 X calls. Fetch page 2 (the next_token page) only when page 1 returned a next_token, at least one page-1 author has a SpaceX or xAI affiliation in their bio, fewer than 3 candidates qualified after applying the add rules to page 1, and the pool is under 35. Page 1 with zero affiliated authors means stop. Otherwise stop after page 1. Bios come from the search expansions; activity comes from the weekly user lookup, so no extra calls.
6. New players get the next tile numbers; dropped players' numbers are retired. New players get no FOUNDER tag unless their bio says founder, co-founder or founding team.
7. Add one recap line under the swap line, exactly: `Pool: +@a, +@b · −@c` (adds, then drops after ` · `; omit a side that is empty), or `Pool: no changes`. If the line would pass the 984px text width, list as many entries as fit, then `+N more`.

## Search query templates
- `<GOAL_OR>` = every query form of every goal word (see Goal stems in the picking rules) joined with OR, in parentheses, no blind plurals. For shift, template, worker: `(shift OR shifts OR template OR templates OR worker OR workers)`. For grow, brand: `(grow OR grows OR brand OR brands)`. For honing, moonshotting: `(hone OR honing OR moonshot OR moonshots OR moonshotting)`. For fine tuning, performance: `("fine tune" OR "fine-tune" OR finetune OR "fine tuning" OR "fine-tuning" OR finetuning OR performance OR performances)`.
- Prefetch query: `<GOAL_OR> (from:h1 OR from:h2 OR ...) -is:retweet -is:reply` over the working-pool handles in pool order, max_results 25 (the most one call returns). If a chunk returns a next_token, do not page: the starters' own posts (weekly run steps 5 and 7) are still fetched in full. 29 from: terms come to about 600 chars, so split: fill chunk 1 with handles in pool order and start a new chunk at the first handle that would push the full query (goal part, from: group and suffix) past 512 chars. For the 29-handle seed and the goal "building Grok Bot templates for shift workers" that split falls before @lingxi (tile 25), giving 2 queries. Every handle appears in exactly one chunk; logo accounts are included (their posts are read, they just are not auto-picked).
- Never send a query without `-is:retweet -is:reply`.

## Presets (2)
Each member's evidence is a verbatim string from their public X bio. Before offering a preset, check each evidence string is still in that player's current bio (case-insensitive) and the handle is in the pool; drop a preset whose starters no longer all check out. Also check activity: a member with no post in the last 30 days (from `most_recent_tweet_id`) is offered tagged `INACTIVE`, with a suggested `out <tile> in <tile>` tweak to an active pool player.

## Weekly starter picking (from the goal)
1. Goal words: lowercase the goal, drop possessive 's, take words of 3+ letters (a hyphenated word such as fine-tuning is one word, never split), fold a trailing plural s (words over 3 letters), and drop generic words: grok, bot, bots, how, why, when, where, who, can, should, get, with, that, this, from, your, their, team, work, working, what, and, the, for, building, build, builds, making, make, about, into, some, more, lots, a, an. Example: "building Grok Bot templates for shift workers" gives shift, template, worker; "how do we grow the brand" gives grow, brand ("grow" is a real goal word, never generic).
   Goal stems (one per goal word, used for matching and for `<GOAL_OR>`):
   - Base form: if the word ends in -ing, drop it and undo a doubled final b, d, g, m, n, p or t (moonshotting -> moonshot); else if it ends in -ed, drop it the same way; strip a suffix only when 3+ letters remain (need stays need). If what remains is 3 letters ending consonant-vowel-consonant (last letter not w, x or y), add back the e (honing -> hone, coding -> code).
   - Stem: the base minus a trailing -e (template -> templat, hone -> hon).
   - Stem of 4+ letters: a post word matches when it starts with the stem at a word boundary and the rest of the word is empty or a known suffix: e, s, es, d, ed, ing, er, ers, th, ly, ment, ments, ness, ion, ions, or a doubled final consonant plus ing, ed, er or ers (ting, ted, ...). So moonshot matches moonshots, moonshotting; grow matches grows, growing, growth, but not growl. Query forms: the base, base + s, and the original goal word if different (moonshot, moonshots, moonshotting).
   - Stem under 4 letters: no prefix match and no added forms (no -s, -ed, -d or -ing). Match exact whole words only: the base and the original goal word (honing gives hone, honing; fine gives fine, so fines and fined do not match; app gives app). Those are also the query forms.
   - Compounds: a hyphenated goal word, or two adjacent goal words that are also commonly written hyphenated or as one word, is one term (fine tuning is one term; ordinary pairs such as shift workers stay separate words). Take its base and stem from the closed form with the rules above (finetuning -> finetun), so it always gets the 4+ letter prefix match, and the join in a post may be a space, a hyphen or nothing: fine-tuning, fine tuning, finetune, finetuning and fine-tuned all match. Query forms (these replace base + s): for the last part's base and for the original goal word, the spaced and hyphenated forms (in quotes) and the closed form (`"fine tune" OR "fine-tune" OR finetune OR "fine tuning" OR "fine-tuning" OR finetuning`).
   - Examples: "how do we grow the brand" gives goal words grow, brand, stems grow, brand. "Honing and moonshotting my team" gives goal words honing, moonshotting ("and", "team" generic, "my" under 3 letters), stems hon (short: hone, honing) and moonshot (prefix). "fine tuning performance" gives goal words fine tuning (one compound term) and performance, stems finetun (compound, prefix) and performanc. "building Grok Bot templates for shift workers" gives stems shift, templat, worker.
   Empty goal: no goal words, so skip every goal-dependent search (pool refresh search and prefetch). The empty-goal rules win over the zero on-topic week rules: no `No on-topic posts this week` line, and exactly 3+3 ideas for "your own work".
2. On-topic post = an original post (not a reply, not a repost) whose text matches a goal stem per the Goal stems rule (prefix match for stems of 4+ letters, exact forms for short stems). A post that only says "bot" is not on-topic. A search match alone is not on-topic: X can match on a link, a handle or an expanded URL, so re-check every returned post's own text (with t.co links removed) against the goal stems before counting it, for prefetch, refresh and posts calls alike.
3. Only pickable players are ranked: every pool player except `initials` accounts (official/logo accounts such as @grok, @bot, @SpaceXSI, @cursor_ai). Logo accounts stay on the board and the user can hand-pick them at setup (by number or preset tweak); a hand-picked one stays through fill/fallback like any last-week starter. They are never auto-picked as starters or bench. Rank pickable players with 1+ on-topic posts by: on-topic post count (high first), then total likes on those on-topic posts (engagement tie-break), then pool number.
4. 5 or more on-topic: top 5 start (mode on-topic). 1 to 4 on-topic: they start, filled from last week's starters in last week's order (mode filled). No starter has an on-topic highlight (zero on-topic week, as defined under Ideas rules), or empty goal: keep last week's 5 starters unchanged (mode fallback). Setup run (`setup`): no picking at all; starters and bench are exactly the just-confirmed `roster_setup` (mode setup), and the swap line is `Lineup changes this week: none (setup roster)`.
   Inactive starters (weekly runs, every mode): a starter with no post in the last 30 days (from `most_recent_tweet_id` in Call 1) does not keep the slot. Replace them, in their slot, with the best-ranked on-topic pickable player not already starting, else the next active pickable player in pool order not on the roster. This applies to hand-picked logo accounts too (a replacement is never a logo account). The replaced starter goes to the pool, not the bench, and shows as `out` on the swap line. Setup runs keep the confirmed roster and only mark such starters `INACTIVE`.
5. Never an empty or short lineup: if still under 5 (first week, no state), fill with pickable players in pool order (mode seed).
6. Bench = on-topic players not starting (ranked), then last week's starters who lost their slot (last week's order), then last week's bench players not starting (last week's order), max 6; anyone past 6 goes back to the pool. This holds in every mode, so filled and fallback weeks keep last week's bench.
7. Recap rows: the BENCH row shows exactly this week's bench (0 to 6). A separate POOL row shows the rest of the working pool (not starting, not bench, no `initials`/logo accounts) in pool order, as many as fit on one line, then `+N more`.
8. Swap line, exactly: `Lineup changes this week: in @a, @b · out @c, @d`, or `Lineup changes this week: none`. Setup-week weekly run (a `weekly` run whose week id matches an existing setup entry and no `weekly` entry exists for that week): append the entry as usual (the setup entry stays), compare against the setup lineup as last week's lineup, and write the swap line as `Lineup changes since setup: in @a · out @c` or `Lineup changes since setup: none`. If a swap line would pass the 984px text width, list as many handles as fit, then `+N more` (same rule as the Pool line), keeping the `in` and `out` labels: cut the longer side first, e.g. `in @a, @b +2 more · out @c +3 more`.

## Lineup state
Keep all state in your own memory under the key `tech-team-draft`, or in a file you create in your own data folder at `tech-team-draft/state.json`. Use one of the two, the same one every week. Shape: `{"pool": [...], "roster_setup": {"preset", "starters", "bench"}, "goal": "...", "weeks": [{"week", "run", "label", "goal", "starters", "bench", "mode", "swap", "pool"}]}`. `run` is `setup` (the first recap at setup) or `weekly`. Saving: if the newest entry has the same week id and both it and this run are `weekly`, replace it (a re-run); otherwise append a new entry, so a setup entry and that week's Sunday run are both kept. Last week's starters and bench always come from the newest entry; with no entry, use roster_setup.
- Goal change: the newest goal the user gave wins. Save it to `goal` right away, and every run stores the goal it used on that week's entry (`weeks[].goal`). A re-run after a goal change replaces that week's entry with the new goal.
- Week id: the date of the Sunday that ends the run date's Monday-to-Sunday week, in the user's timezone, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. A Thursday Oct 15 2026 setup and the Sunday Oct 18 2026 run both get `2026-10-18` (the setup entry is kept and the Sunday entry is appended after it). Do not use ISO week numbers.
- Week label (shown on the recap): `WEEK OF <MON> <D> <YYYY>` for the first day of the 7-day window, uppercase month (a Sunday Oct 18 2026 run is `WEEK OF OCT 11 2026`).

## Highlights
- A starter's highlight is their most-liked on-topic post this week, from their own posts or from this week's prefetch results; if they have no on-topic post, their most-liked post. Ties: the newest post.
- Excerpt: first remove every t.co link (`https://t.co/...`), then strip emoji, then take the first 20 words verbatim (links never use a word slot), and end with `…` when the post was longer. Link https://x.com/<handle>/status/<id>. Zero posts: `quiet week`, no highlight.

## Ideas rules
- Count only on-topic highlights. 3 or more on-topic starters: exactly 3 sharper ideas (small, doable this week) and 3 stretch ideas (bigger). 1 or 2 on-topic starters: ideas only from those highlights, at most 1 sharper and 1 stretch each, no padding from off-topic posts.
- Each idea is one short line tied to one real highlight from this week: it names that player as @handle and uses a goal word (any word that matches a goal stem per the Goal stems rule). "bot" alone never counts as on-topic, since it is a generic word.
- Reuse: a highlight may back at most 2 ideas, one sharper and one stretch; never two ideas in the same group from one highlight. Prefer 6 different highlights when there are 6.
- Zero on-topic week (no starter has an on-topic highlight): show the line `No on-topic posts this week` under the Pool line, and give only ideas that quote or paraphrase the highlight post itself and use a goal word: 0 to 3 sharper and 0 to 3 stretch. If none fits honestly, give 0 ideas. Never force 3+3 that week. With 0 ideas, the IDEAS block is the label `IDEAS` followed by the line `No on-topic posts this week`.
- Empty goal: ideas are for "your own work" and need no goal word.
- No idea from a quiet or not-found player. No facts beyond the quoted posts.
- Before showing, check: 3+3 (fewer on a week with 0 to 2 on-topic starters, as above), each ref has a highlight, each names its @handle, each uses a goal word, reuse limit held. Fix and re-check on any miss.

## Weekly run (up to 25 X calls)
1. Load the lineup state (memory or the state file). Check the roster against the Rules; stop on any error. Compute the week id and label.
2. Call 1: get_users_by_usernames with all working-pool handles plus any retired seed players in one batch, user.fields description,name,username,public_metrics,profile_image_url,most_recent_tweet_id. Keep each user's numeric `id`.
3. Pool refresh per the refresh rules (max 2 calls). Save the new pool and its `Pool:` line.
4. Prefetch (max 2 calls): the prefetch query chunks per the search query templates, last 7 days, expansions author_id, post.fields created_at,public_metrics,in_reply_to_user_id. No pagination.
5. Fetch last week's roster: get_users_posts for each last-week starter before picking.
6. Pick this week's starters from the refreshed pool with the picking rules (prefetch hits + step 5 posts), then record the lineup state and build the swap line.
7. Then fetch get_users_posts for each new starter (a starter who was not a starter last week), so every starter has a full week of posts.
   Every get_users_posts fetch: `id` = the numeric user id from Call 1 (not the handle), start_time 7 days ago, end_time now, max_results 25 (the most one call returns), exclude replies,retweets, post.fields created_at,public_metrics. If the response has a next_token, fetch the next page (at most 2 pages per player). The count is exact only when the window is covered: the last page has no next_token and either returned fewer than 15 posts or its oldest post is within a day of start_time (X can drop filtered posts from a full page without giving a token). Otherwise show `N+ posts` with N = posts received.
8. Highlights per the highlight rules; ideas by the ideas rules.
9. Render the recap per the rendering spec; markdown card if rendering fails.

## Call math
1 user lookup + up to 2 refresh + up to 2 prefetch + up to 10 starters (5 last-week + up to 5 new) x up to 2 pages = 25 max, under a 30 per run budget. Usually 1 page each, so about 10 to 15. On a 429, wait for x-rate-limit-reset, retry that call once, then mark the player `no data`.

## Setup
First-run setup (draft board, presets, picks, tweaks, goal question, first recap, paused schedule) is the **tech-team-draft-getting-started** skill, which ships with this one. If there is no lineup state yet, run that skill first. Everything the weekly run needs is in this file.

## Recap rendering (write it at runtime, nothing is shipped)
Write a small Python script with Pillow (`pip install pillow` if missing) from this spec, run it, and show the PNG(s).
- Colors: background #0a0a0a. Cards #161616 with a 1px #2a2a2a border, 16px radius. Text white #ffffff; secondary text gray #9a9a9a; one accent #3898ff only for like counts and the STARTER tag.
- Fonts: download Space Grotesk from Google Fonts (`https://github.com/google/fonts/raw/main/ofl/spacegrotesk/SpaceGrotesk%5Bwght%5D.ttf`) to a temp folder; if that fails use `ImageFont.load_default(size=...)`. Kicker in a monospace font if one is installed, else the same font. Render at 2x, all sizes below are 1x.
- Emoji: the font has no emoji, so strip emoji (and variation selectors / zero-width joiners) from every name, quote and idea before drawing. Never draw a tofu box.
- Recap canvas 1080 wide, max 1350 tall (4:5), 48px outer margin, 12px gap between starter cards. Top to bottom: kicker `TECH TEAM DRAFT · <week label>` (mono, gray, 22px; on the setup first recap it is `TECH TEAM DRAFT · <week label> (setup preview)`, before any `· 1 of 2`; the setup board's kicker is `TECH TEAM DRAFT · DRAFT BOARD (setup preview)`, see Board canvas); title `FOR: <goal>` (or `FOR: your own work`, 40px, one line, cut with `…`); the swap line, then the `Pool:` line (18px gray), then `No on-topic posts this week` (18px gray) only on a zero on-topic week; 5 starter cards 118px tall (avatar circle 72px, name 22px, @handle 17px gray, STARTER tag top right (with `INACTIVE` in 13px gray just left of it for a starter with no post in 30 days, which only happens on a setup recap), highlight excerpt in quotes max 2 lines 17px, then the stats line: like count `N likes` in accent #3898ff, then ` · N posts` (` · 1 post` when N = 1, ` · N+ posts` when the window was not covered) in gray #9a9a9a right after it on the same line (this week's post count from get_users_posts), or `quiet week` / `no data`); then 24px pad; BENCH label (16px gray, 24px) and row (36px avatars + handles, this week's bench only, 44px); 12px pad; POOL label and row (same sizes, rest of the pool without logo accounts; add avatar + handle items left to right while they fit within 1080 - 2 x 48 px, keeping room for the `+N more` label, then `+N more` for the rest); 12px pad; IDEAS · SHARPER then IDEAS · STRETCH, 3 one-liners each (17px; each group = 24px label + 3 x 26px + 8px); footer `Unofficial fan template` (gray, 18px).
- Vertical budget (1x px): 48 margin + 40 kicker + 60 FOR + 28 swap + 28 Pool + 8 pad + 5 x 118 cards + 4 x 12 gaps + 24 + 24 + 44 bench + 12 + 24 + 44 pool + 12 + 220 ideas + 40 footer + 48 margin = 1342, under 1350. With 24px gaps it would be 1390 and overflow, so keep the gaps at 12. A zero on-topic week adds the 28px `No on-topic posts this week` line: with 3+3 ideas that is 1370 and splits into 1 of 2 / 2 of 2; with fewer ideas it usually fits.
- Single-image crop rule: if everything fits, the image height = footer bottom + 48px margin (never taller than 1350, never an empty band above the footer). If the content would pass 1350, split into two images, each cropped the same way. The marker goes in the kicker: `TECH TEAM DRAFT · <week label> · 1 of 2` and `... · 2 of 2`. Image 1: everything except the ideas. Image 2 repeats only the kicker and the FOR line, then the ideas and the footer (no swap, Pool, starter, BENCH or POOL rows).
- Board canvas (setup): 1080 wide, height = 48 + 60 + rows x (150 + 24) - 24 + 48 + 30 where rows = ceil(tiles / 4) (29 tiles = 1080x1554). Kicker `TECH TEAM DRAFT · DRAFT BOARD (setup preview)` at the top, 4 columns of 150px #161616 tiles, each with the tile number top left (18px gray), a 56px avatar centered, name (17px), @handle (15px gray), FOUNDER (13px) where backed, `INACTIVE` (13px gray) for no post in the last 30 days, STARTER/BENCH (accent) once drafted; footer `Unofficial fan template`. One image. After the user's picks are confirmed, re-render the board with the STARTER/BENCH tags and show it again.
- Avatars: fetch at runtime from each user's `profile_image_url` (swap `_normal` for `_400x400`) with a browser User-Agent header, `Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/124.0 Safari/537.36` (the image host answers 403 without one); crop to a circle. On any fetch error, or for `initials` players, draw a #2a2a2a circle with the first 2 letters of the handle. Never reuse another player's photo.
- If Pillow, the font, or the script fails at any step: send a markdown card instead with the same sections (kicker, FOR line, swap line, Pool line, starters table, BENCH line, POOL line, ideas list, footer). Never skip the recap.
- Under the image(s), list each highlight link as text: https://x.com/<handle>/status/<id>.

# Tech Team Draft: getting started

Setup only. The shared sections live in the weekly **tech-team-draft** skill and are not repeated here: Rules, Player pool seed, Presets, Search query templates, Weekly pool refresh, Weekly starter picking, Lineup state, Highlights, Ideas rules, Weekly run, and Recap rendering (including the board canvas spec). Load the tech-team-draft skill and follow those sections exactly. If it is not installed, say so and stop.

## Setup-only rules
- Read-only on X: only the built-in read-only `x` tools that the tech-team-draft skill allows. Never post, reply, like, repost, follow, bookmark or DM.
- Every handle comes from the tech-team-draft skill's pool seed. Never add one from memory.

## Setup steps
1. Draft board: one get_users_by_usernames call for the 29 pool handles with user.fields description,name,username,profile_image_url,public_metrics,most_recent_tweet_id. This same response is Call 1 of the first recap (save it; don't call again). Show numbered tiles 1 to 29 in pool order per the tech-team-draft skill's board canvas spec, kicker `TECH TEAM DRAFT · DRAFT BOARD (setup preview)`: avatar fetched at runtime (initials for `initials` players or on fetch error), name, @handle, FOUNDER tag only where that skill's pool seed has bio evidence still in the current bio, `INACTIVE` tag for no post in the last 30 days. Markdown numbered list if rendering fails.
2. Offer the 2 presets from the tech-team-draft skill as one-tap rosters with their tile numbers, after checking their evidence against the live bios and their activity (an inactive member is shown `INACTIVE` with a suggested tweak).
3. The user picks one of: a preset name; numbers like "1, 4, 7, 9, 12" then optional "bench 2, 15"; or a tweak on a preset written `out 3 in 12` (tile 3 leaves, tile 12 takes its slot). Echo every tweak before applying it, exactly `Out: 3 @<handle> · In: 12 @<handle> (starter slot). Confirm?` (or `bench slot`), and apply only after a yes. Older wording such as "swap 3 for 12" is not accepted: reply `Say it as: out <tile> in <tile>, e.g. out 3 in 12.` Refuse 6+ starters, 7+ bench, duplicates, a tile already on the roster, an out tile not on the roster, and numbers outside the board; show the error and ask again.
4. Re-render the board with STARTER/BENCH tags for the confirmed picks and show it (tech-team-draft board canvas spec).
5. Save the working pool (a copy of the seed) and the roster as `roster_setup` in the lineup state defined by the tech-team-draft skill (same memory key or state file).
6. Ask one question: "What's your team working on?" (one line, max 120 chars). Save it as the goal. Blank is fine: ideas then use "your own work".
7. First recap now, before scheduling: do the tech-team-draft skill's weekly run steps once (read-only calls only, reusing the board response as Call 1; first run, so no pool drops), using the confirmed roster exactly, inactive starters included and tagged `INACTIVE` (no picking or swaps at setup; swap line `Lineup changes this week: none (setup roster)`), save it with run `setup`, and show it with the kicker `TECH TEAM DRAFT · <week label> (setup preview)`.
8. Suggest Sunday 8:00am in the user's timezone. Create the weekly routine for the tech-team-draft skill at that time, PAUSED. Only a plain yes ("yes", "ok", "sure") turns it on. Another time replaces the default and is still created paused.

## Don't
- Don't post, like, follow or DM anyone on X.
- Don't add a handle that isn't in the tech-team-draft pool seed.
- Don't give a preset or tile a role its bio evidence doesn't back.
- Don't turn the routine on without a yes.
